global_caption: A miniature forest stage is composed of oversized bread trees, cookie bushes, and candy vines. The overall visuals are dominated by soft natural lighting, with a jam-colored backlight at dusk in the closing moments.
shot1: Shot 1 begins with a fade-in, using a wide overhead composition. The waffle clearing is centered, surrounded by towering bread trees and cookie shrubs forming a natural embrace. In the foreground, edges of lettuce leaves are gently moved by the wind; in the background, winding candy vines and slightly reflective candy wrappers are visible. He walks slowly, his shoes pressing lightly into the crumbly ground, creating subtle displacement. His clothing and straps flutter slightly in the breeze. The camera performs a slow downward overhead dolly-in. The rustling wind
shot2: Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot to a close-up eye-level view. The composition places a cookie tree root at the bottom of the frame as a natural seat. The boy child sits slightly off-center to the right. The background retains soft bread tree trunk textures. Lighting remains warm and soft with slight dappled patterns from leaf gaps. He places the guitar steadily on his lap, lightly plucks a test note, lifts his head, inhales slightly, and clearly enunciates "One, two, three, four. As the count-in ends, his right hand gently touches the strings. Wind
shot3: The guitar body is centered visually. Shallow depth of field blurs the background candy vines into soft color blocks. Warm light creates fine reflections on the wooden guitar surface. He begins formal playing. Right-hand strumming shifts from tentative to steady and strong. On the first downbeat, his shoulders slightly lift his upper body. Sleeve edges and hair tips move with the motion.
shot4: Shot 4 connects via a quick match cut to an extreme close-up overhead shot. Focus is on the left hand and fretboard. Background is heavily blurred, with only warm candy wrapper reflections as point accents. Lighting remains natural and warm, with slight highlights on fingertips. The left hand slides between frets, changes chords, pauses briefly, then quickly lands. Subtle deformation of fingertips pressing strings and visible string vibration are apparent. The camera performs a minimal overhead pan following finger paths.
shot5: Using a slightly low-angle eye-level perspective, the boy and surrounding candy vines enter the frame together. Semi-transparent candy wrappers occasionally pass in the foreground. The midground shows the performing figure. The background features wind-lifted candy vines and cookie shrubs. Overall warmth intensifies, lighting begins transitioning toward dusk but maintains consistent softness. Right-hand strums become broader. The camera moves in a half-circular orbit around the subject, speed increasing in sync with the Ambient wind
shot6: Shot 6 concludes with a fade-out pull-back from the previous shot, cutting to a wide backlight pull-out. The camera starts at a slightly low angle, then gradually rises to a stable distant view. The boy and waffle clearing are placed within a broader jam-colored twilight. Distant oversized bread trees are outlined with soft glowing edges by backlighting. Candy vines and lettuce leaves remain as slowly swaying silhouettes. The central composition still features the seated figure holding the guitar, but its proportion gradually diminishes. After completing the final concluding strum, he stops playing, fingers still lightly pressing the neck to let the final note linger naturally. The camera continues a steady pull-out, allowing the final note to fade into twilight. Ultimately, only the rustling of wind through lettuce leaves and candy wrappers remains, concluding the piece.
